channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Bishkek landfill fire prompts security enhancement plans
item.description: A fire at Bishkek's sanitary landfill, originating from four locations with tires, is under investigation. Security measures, including fencing and access restrictions, are in place and will be strengthened with additional cameras. The waste processing plant operates normally, with plans for expansion to increase capacity and power generation.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev and German President Steinmeier Hold Expanded Talks
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and German Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier held expanded negotiations. Tokayev expressed gratitude for the invitation to Germany, noting the high level of contacts signifies strategic bilateral cooperation. Germany is a key European partner for Kazakhstan, with strong friendship and mutual trust.

item.title: Krygyzneftegaz Corruption Case: Commission to Recalculate Damages
item.description: A commission is being appointed to recalculate the damages caused to the state in the Krygyzneftegaz corruption case. The defense requested the recalculation due to unclear and inaccurate aspects regarding the amount of damage. Former MP Shairbek Tashiev, accused in the scheme, was released under house arrest after repaying most of the alleged damages.

item.title: Astana Court Sentences Clinic Officials for Embezzling 672 Million Tenge
item.description: A court in Astana has sentenced clinic officials for embezzling 672 million tenge. The group is accused of siphoning funds for personal use, including luxury travel and loan payments, between 2021 and 2025. The total damage to the state enterprise was substantial.

item.title: Moody's Affirms Kazakhstan's Economy at 'Baa1' with a Stable Outlook
item.description: Moody's has affirmed Kazakhstan's economic rating at 'Baa1' with a stable outlook, citing strong fiscal standing, low public debt, and high debt servicing capacity. Despite a decline in oil production, the economy continues to grow due to non-oil sectors, supported by infrastructure investments and tax reforms.

item.title: Fergana Valley Must Become Space for Peace and Shared Development, Says Eldor Aripov
item.description: Eldor Aripov, Director of the Institute for Strategic and Regional Studies, stated at the Second Fergana Valley Peace Forum that the region should become a space for peace, trust, and shared development. The forum aims to transition from mutual understanding to joint initiatives and projects among Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Tajikistan.

item.title: Successful agricultural practices to be expanded across Karakalpakstan
item.description: Uzbekistan's President has emphasized the agricultural sector's importance. A 55 billion soum intensive orchard project in Kegeyli district, covering 330 hectares with salt-resistant plum saplings and water-saving irrigation, is a successful example. This experience will be replicated across Karakalpakstan, aiming for 10,000 hectares of intensive gardens and creating 40,000 jobs.

item.title: Janaozen Workers Protest, Military Reforms, and Caspian Sea Incidents
item.description: Dozens of workers in Janaozen protested and sought President Tokayev's help. Online users are sharing experiences from military service following a death in the Caspian Sea. Students in France protested, and Hungary repealed a law preventing prosecution of its prime minister.

item.title: Kazakhstan Achieves Best Global Innovation Index Result in a Decade, Ranking 73rd
item.description: Kazakhstan has climbed eight places to 73rd out of 139 economies in the 2026 Global Innovation Index, its best performance in ten years. The country also secured first place in Central Asia and second among 11 Central and South Asian economies. Its innovation output sub-index improved by 11 positions.

item.title: Central Asian Nations Propose Mutual Recognition of Electronic Signatures
item.description: Central Asian countries have proposed mutual recognition of electronic signatures and simplification of cross-border payments to reduce digital barriers. Discussions also included creating a common ethical code for responsible AI use, emphasizing human accountability and transparency in AI interactions. The code will be recommendatory.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Germany Presidents hold talks in narrow format
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier held talks. Tokayev highlighted Germany's role as a key strategic partner and noted 35 years of diplomatic relations. Steinmeier praised Tokayev's contribution to cooperation.

item.title: Kazakh citizens fined for spreading fake news about Caspian Sea tragedy
item.description: Several Kazakh citizens were fined 86,500 tenge for spreading false information on social media about a tragedy in the Caspian Sea. Police identified users who posted unverified claims about a serviceman's actions during the incident, which the Ministry of Defense refuted.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister and UK Defence Minister discuss sanctions evasion
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister Jeenbek Kulubaev met with UK Minister of State for Defence Lord Vernon Coaker. Kulubaev informed the British side about efforts to prevent sanctions evasion and stressed the importance of providing updated information. They also discussed economic cooperation and critical minerals.

item.title: Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Discusses Sanctions Prevention with UK Defense Minister
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Foreign Minister, Jeenbek Kulubaev, met with Lord Vernon Coaker, the UK Minister for Defence Procurement. The discussion focused on preventing sanctions. The meeting took place between the two high-ranking officials.

item.title: Uzbekistan: 22 Pupils Hospitalized After Cotton Field Spraying Near School
item.description: Twenty-two pupils in southern Uzbekistan were hospitalized after chemicals were sprayed on a cotton field beside their school. Seven remained hospitalized as of September 29, while 15 had been discharged. The Interior Ministry stated the farm used Agro Augron, a chemical applied to make cotton plants shed leaves. A criminal case has been opened.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Electrical Industry Achieves Growth and New Opportunities
item.description: Uzbekistan's electrical industry has seen significant growth, becoming a key player in the international market. Production volume increased from 1.665 trillion soms ten years ago to 30 trillion soms in the first seven months of this year. Exports now reach 65 countries, driven by focus on development, incentives, and a rich raw material base.

item.title: Manas City's Power Capacity to Increase by 25 Megawatts
item.description: The power capacity of Manas city will increase by 25 megawatts, according to the Jalal-Abad Electric Networks enterprise. Over 2,700 new subscribers were connected in 2025, with an additional 1,254 connected by May 2026. Approximately 4,000 more subscribers are expected by year-end. Extensive repair work is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Temperature Rising Twice as Fast as Global Average Over 50 Years
item.description: Kazakhstan's average annual temperature has risen by 0.4 degrees Celsius per decade since 1976, roughly twice the global average. This warming is more pronounced in mid- and high-latitude regions like Kazakhstan, far from oceanic moderating effects. Spring temperatures are increasing fastest, at 0.7 degrees per decade.

item.title: Suspect extradited from Russia for defrauding three people of over 106 million tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office extradited a citizen from Russia for alleged fraud. The suspect is accused of defrauding three victims of over 106 million tenge by falsely promising to import vehicles between 2021 and 2022. He was placed on an international wanted list after fleeing and was recently apprehended in Russia.

item.title: Taliban detain former official and his son in Kandahar
item.description: Local sources in Kandahar report that the Taliban have arrested Gul Mohammad Shakran, the former head of anti-narcotics for the province, and his son, Nazir Ahmad Shakran. They were reportedly detained by Taliban security forces and are being held for investigation. Relatives confirm Shakran had been interrogated by the Taliban previously.

item.title: Moody's Affirms Stable Outlook for Kazakhstan's Credit Rating
item.description: Moody's has affirmed Kazakhstan's sovereign credit rating at 'Baa1' with a 'Stable' outlook, according to the Ministry of National Economy. The agency cited the country's strong fiscal position, low public debt, and accumulated foreign exchange assets. Growth is expected to continue, driven by non-oil sectors and infrastructure investments.

item.title: Taliban Summons Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires Over Border Incursions into Nuristan
item.description: The Taliban's Foreign Ministry summoned Pakistan's Chargé d'Affaires in Kabul to protest armed elements crossing the Durand Line into Nuristan. The ministry condemned Pakistan's alleged support for these elements, calling it a violation of Afghanistan's sovereignty. Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting denied any involvement.

item.title: Former Deputy Police Chief's Driver Sentenced for Fatal Al-Farabi Accident
item.description: A former driver for Almaty's deputy police chief has been sentenced to three years and six months in prison for dereliction of duty leading to a fatal traffic accident. The court also permanently barred him from public service. He was found guilty of knowing about the driver's intoxication and dangerous driving but failing to intervene.

item.title: Almaty Considers Expanding Low Emission Zone Citywide
item.description: Almaty is considering extending its Low Emission Zone (LEZ) to cover the entire city. Currently in a pilot phase, the LEZ aims to reduce transport emissions. Future regulations could impose stricter rules for drivers, potentially increasing costs for owners of older vehicles.

item.title: Water from Aktobe Reservoir Tested After Bird and Fish Die-offs
item.description: Water samples from the Aktobe Reservoir are undergoing laboratory analysis following reports of dead birds and fish. Local residents posted videos of carcasses. An environmental department working group, including various ecological and veterinary bodies, has collected samples for investigation. No mass die-offs have been identified.

item.title: Iran Warns of Middle East Infrastructure Threat if Oil Exports Halted
item.description: Iran's chief negotiator, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, warned that if the Islamic Republic cannot export oil, no one else will. He further cautioned that all infrastructure in the Middle East would be at risk if the security of the Islamic Republic is not guaranteed.

item.title: Low Emission Zone in Almaty May Expand to Cover Entire City
item.description: Following a pilot project, there is a proposal to expand Almaty's Low Emission Zone (LEZ) to the entire city. The head of the atmospheric air protection working group stated that expanding the LEZ is necessary due to Almaty's geographical location hindering pollutant dispersal. A separate decree from the city administration is required to implement the expansion.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Germany Presidents Hold Talks in Restricted Format
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev thanked German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier for the invitation to Germany and hospitality. Tokayev highlighted Germany as Kazakhstan's main strategic partner in Europe, with cooperation based on mutual trust and common interests. They noted the upcoming 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations and expressed confidence that the visit would boost bilateral ties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China Sign Energy Cooperation Agreement
item.description: The Ministry of Energy of the Kyrgyz Republic and the National Energy Administration of China have signed an agreement to cooperate in the energy sector.

item.title: New Polyclinic and Ambulatory Surgery Center to Be Built in Shymkent
item.description: A new polyclinic with a capacity of 500 visits per shift will be constructed in the Shymkent City microdistrict, serving over 30,000 residents. The facility will include adult and pediatric departments, a family health center, emergency care, diagnostics, and an ambulatory surgery center.

item.title: Kazakhstan Men's Water Polo Team Reaches Asian Games Semifinals
item.description: The Kazakhstan men's national water polo team has advanced to the semifinals of the Asian Games after defeating South Korea 18-14 in the quarterfinals. Kazakhstan is a strong contender in Asian water polo and has consistently competed for top honors.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Holds Talks with German Federal President Steinmeier
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev met with German Federal President Frank-Walter Steinmeier in Astana. Tokayev highlighted Germany as a key European strategic partner, emphasizing mutual trust and shared interests. The leaders discussed strengthening bilateral cooperation ahead of the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations next year.

item.title: Taliban Summons Pakistan's Envoy Over Alleged Border Incursion in Nuristan
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Pakistan's chargé d'affaires in Kabul to lodge a protest over alleged incursions by armed elements into Nuristan province. The ministry claimed Pakistani militias supported groups crossing the Durand Line to create insecurity, with Pakistani military personnel allegedly involved.

item.title: Ghor Province Governor's Office Attacked; Taliban Claims Attacker Killed, Child Injured
item.description: Taliban security forces in Ghor confirmed an explosive device detonated near the entrance of the provincial governor's office. The Taliban spokesperson stated the attacker was killed and one child was injured. An opposing group, the United Afghanistan Front, claimed responsibility, reporting one Taliban guard killed and eight injured.

item.title: Uzbekistan to develop separate system for girls' chess and para-chess
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to create a separate system for developing girls' chess and para-chess. The initiative aims to identify talented children early in every region, district, and neighborhood, assign them to strong coaches, and facilitate their participation in international tournaments.

item.title: Taliban closes Afghan Voice Agency office and arrests journalist, says media watchdog
item.description: The Afghanistan Journalists Center condemned the Taliban's closure of Afghan Voice Agency's Kabul office and the arrest of one of its journalists. The Ministry of Justice reportedly shut down the agency's offices last Thursday. The Taliban have not yet provided an explanation for the actions.

item.title: Dushanbe introduces unified utility payment system for electricity, water, and heating
item.description: Dushanbe is launching a new unified system for paying utility bills, combining electricity, water, and heating charges. The system aims to simplify the payment process for residents. Details on how the new service will operate are being provided.

item.title: Taliban Deputy Governor in Khwahan Accused of Land Grabs and Extorting Miners
item.description: Residents of Khwahan District accuse Taliban deputy governor Amanuddin Mohammadi of seizing state and private land, distributing it to miners, and extorting money. His associates allegedly harass residents and embezzle funds from land and mining site seizures.

item.title: Afghan minister visits Belarus to boost economic and trade ties
item.description: Afghanistan's Minister of Industry and Commerce, Nooruddin Azizi, is in Belarus leading a delegation to strengthen economic and trade cooperation. The visit includes attending the Second Belarus International Industrial Exhibition and holding meetings with Belarusian officials to discuss trade, investment, and cooperation.

item.title: Kabul women face double fares and refusal of service on public transport
item.description: Women and girls in Kabul report facing restrictions and problems on public transport, including drivers refusing service or demanding double fares. They state that gender-based restrictions extend to social services, forcing women to pay more and endure longer waits for transport.
